text:
zoe: quick heads-up  I routed mercury-int6 to staging canary (15%) and the short-span spanish cohort (<=20 tokens) shows a weird Recall@5 dip. noticed this in the dashboard heatmap :confused:

infra-bot: deploy done  mercury-int6 @staging (canary 15%). view: https://console.redwood.ai/staging/models/mercury/variants/int6

sam: ran a quick recall sweep against the short-span holdout. command:
```bash
./tools/eval_knn.py --model mercury-int6 --queries holdout/short_span_es.json --k 5 --out /tmp/mercury_int6_short_es.txt
```
snippet:
```text
Recall@5: 0.78
Baseline (atlas-v3): 0.86
Churn@5: 0.14
```

jess: dropping per-lang short results from my run (same seed, small N):
```text
lang  baseline  mercury-int6  delta
es    0.86      0.77          -0.09
pt    0.84      0.75          -0.09
en    0.88      0.85          -0.03
```

leo: thats large. I also ran an embed-diff on 500 anchors between atlas-v3 and mercury-int6. mean cosine drop ~0.04 but for short-span ES tokens the drop is ~0.12. attached uvap/umap plots (in ticket). could be quantization pushing clusters apart for short suffixes.

marta: fwiw mercury-int6 used an aggressive per-tensor 6-bit quant config from the new quant pipeline. we have an int8 per-channel build (mercury-int8_pc) sitting in staging but not traffic. worth toggling.

zoe: prefer a no-redeploy flip if possible so we can A/B quickly.

devex-bot: you can split traffic via CLI. example:
```bash
redwood model set-variant --model mercury --variant int8_pc --traffic 10 --env staging
redwood route add-rule --model mercury --condition "tokens <= 20 and lang in [\"es\",\"pt\"]" --variant int8_pc --env staging
```

sam: added 10% traffic to mercury-int8_pc and an explicit routing rule for short-span es/pt. re-ran the eval against the int8_pc slice (same file).

sam: int8_pc results:
```text
Recall@5: 0.84
Baseline (atlas-v3): 0.86
Churn@5: 0.06
lang deltas: es -0.02, pt -0.01
```

jess: nice recovery. can we also run a larger KNN churn measurement (N=10k) and a centroid drift test across languages? also check false positive nearest neighbors id-flip rate.

leo: started overnight batch: 10k stratified short queries (es/pt/en) to compare mercury-int6 vs int8_pc vs atlas-v3. saving nearest neighbor lists and cosine deltas.

marta: performance note  int8_pc increases p95 latency by ~4ms in staging on the sample traffic. cost delta negligible compared to int6 for our infra, but check dedicated numbers.

zoe: rollout proposal if overnight looks good:
- keep int6 as default for long queries (>64 tokens) for cost reasons
- route short-span es/pt queries to int8_pc for 24h canary at 25% traffic
- add recall@5 regression alert threshold of 0.04 absolute drop per language
- run clustering stability (UMAP silhouette) and id-flip tests as part of canary monitors

marta: +1. I'll add a monitoring job and a dashboard tile for churn at K=1/5 and centroid cosine drift per-lang.

jess: also add a synthetic-anchor stress test that modifies short suffix tokens to see sensitivity (helps detect brittle subword interactions).

sam: FYI the eval logs and UMAP pngs will be attached to RED-3551. posting results here once batch finishes.

zoe: thanks team. scheduling 20m sync 11:00 PT tomorrow to review batch. if anyone sees severe customer signals, we can flip routing back in <5m via devex CLI. :thumbsup:
